content: Kerry Prendergast, born on March 28, 1953, has served as the Mayor of Wellington since 2001. She is the second woman to hold this position in the city's history. Kerry Prendergast's professional background lies in the healthcare sector. She is a registered nurse and worked as a midwife for 25 years. She continued her midwifery practice alongside her responsibilities in local government until 2001. Additionally, she has volunteered as a grief counselor. She holds a Master of Business Administration degree from Victoria University of Wellington. Kerry is married and has two daughters and one son. Her husband, Rex Nicholls, operates a property development company in Wellington. Prendergast has had a long and distinguished career in local government. She began her political journey in 1986 as a councilor for the Tawa Borough. In 1989, she was elected to the Wellington City Council and has been re-elected every three years since then. In 1995, she became Deputy Mayor under Mark Blumsky. During the 1999 general election, she ran as a National Party list candidate, ranked 30th on the party's list. However, the National Party did not secure enough votes for her to enter Parliament. She considered running again in the 2002 election, but in 2001, Mark Blumsky announced he would not seek re-election as Mayor and endorsed Prendergast as his successor. She is running for re-election as Mayor in the October 2007 local body elections. During her tenure as Mayor, Prendergast introduced the policy of branding Wellington as the Creative Capital. She has also supported changing the flag of New Zealand. Kerry Prendergast is actively involved in voluntary work. She serves as Vice President of Local Government New Zealand and is a trustee of the Joe Aspell Trust and the New Zealand International Festival of the Arts. She is an honorary life member of the Katherine Mansfield Birthplace Society. As Mayor, she is a patron of several Wellington organizations and holds directorships with Wellington International Airport Limited and the Wellington Region Association of Midwives.
